# Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0504a)

**ID:** Atk S0504a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Commentary on the Itivuttaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*, also known as the *Paramatthadīpanī II* (or *Paramattha-Dīpanī*), is the commentary on the *Itivuttaka* belonging to the Khuddakanikāya commentary collection [Karashima 2012; Dhammadinna 2014]. It is authored by the commentator Ācariya Dhammapāla, who explicitly records in the prologue that his exegesis was composed in strict conformity with the Mahāvihāra tradition [Karashima 2012; Endo 1997]. The work contains an extensive commentary on the opening *nidāna* formula [Almogi 2014], detailed etymological expositions of titles and epithets such as *Bhagavā* and *Tathāgata*, and structured numerical listings of the virtues of the Buddha (*buddha-guṇa*) [Endo 1997]. Its explanations of doctrinal formulas and terms were regarded as authoritative in the Theravāda commentarial tradition; for example, the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* refers readers directly to both the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* for unabridged treatments of the epithet *Tathāgata* [Endo 1997].

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal overlap, recording 66,093 matching passages shared across 574 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest levels of reuse occur with other major Theravāda commentaries and sub-commentaries, most notably the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* (over 251,000 characters), Dhammapāla's companion commentary *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* (over 224,000 characters, with segment matches exhibiting similarity up to 0.96), the *Aṅguttaranikāye Dukanipāta-ṭīkā*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with a match score of 10 or greater are recorded [DharmaNexus]. The text was critically edited for the Pali Text Society by M. M. Bose in two volumes, with indexes prepared by Hermann Kopp [Karashima 2012; Endo 1997; Langer 2007].
